Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those games that constantly reminds me of how amazing it could have been.

The world looks incredible, the atmosphere is fantastic, and the presentation is genuinely top-tier. But the moment you start looking past the shiny exterior, it all starts falling apart.

The story is absolute dogshit. I'd genuinely rather have had the writers of Twilight or The Hunger Games take a crack at it. Stuffing Hollywood celebrities into the game feels less like meaningful storytelling and more like a self-insert fantasy from some "big brain" who thinks their setting is the greatest thing ever conceived.

The gunplay is clunky enough to constantly pull you out of the immersion, and the NPC behaviour is so railroaded and comically reactive that the supposedly living, breathing world quickly starts feeling like a glorified theme park.

And that's what frustrates me most. Every time I give this game another shot, I see glimpses of something genuinely brilliant buried underneath all the self-indulgence. If it had been just a little less concerned with showing off how cool it thinks it is, and a little more focused on actually being a good game, it could have been something special.

I bought Cyberpunk because everyone keeps saying how good the game has become, and honestly, I was just bored out of my mind.

The entire gameplay loop feels like:

Dialogue → walk for 30 seconds → dialogue → walk for another 30 seconds → dialogue → shoot some enemies with some of the worst gunplay I've ever experienced → dialogue → walk for 30 seconds → repeat.

It's just so unbelievably boring.

Don't get me wrong, some of the dialogue is actually interesting, and I can see the appeal of certain story moments. But especially during gameplay missions, the conversations feel incredibly shallow. Characters keep talking at you while you're walking from one objective to another, but most of it feels like filler rather than anything genuinely interesting.

And then there's the dialogue system. You get multiple dialogue options, but most of them feel completely pointless. If you don't pick the obvious main story option, you don't discover anything interesting, unlock a side quest, or get any meaningful alternative outcome. You just get a few extra lines of dialogue before the game forces you back onto the one option that actually progresses the story.

Why even give me the illusion of choice if nothing meaningful comes out of it?

I genuinely don't understand why people enjoy this game so much. Maybe the story gets better later on, but if the gameplay is this tedious, the gunplay feels this bad, and so many dialogue choices feel superficial, I really don't see the appeal.

In terms of worldbuilding and atmosphere, Cyberpunk 2077 might be one of the best games ever. If you're looking for a very story rich game or like Keanu Reeves this is a must play. But the endless dialogue scenes and especially the braindance missions really interrupt the action. Gameplay itself is cool and allows for a lot of customisability, but even on 'very hard' I find it rather easy to just blast through everything before enemies can touch you. If you upgrade your character a bit along the way, it is very easy to simply ignore mechanics. Boss battles are hit or miss, most are simple bullet sponges with high health pools, but some have cool interactions. Side missions are where it's at, definitely don't skip those for both engaging fights and immersive story.

This game is a work of art. With an immersive world and thrilling story. The base game itself is already amazing and the dlc just adds onto that. It has high replayability and customization so no playthrough is exactly the same as your last unless you intend for it to be.

CD Projekt Red never fails to deliver a masterclass in storytelling, and Cyberpunk 2077 stands as an absolute must-play experience.

From the moment you step into Night City, the game pulls you into a beautifully constructed dystopian world. The overarching narrative unfolds gradually, paired with deep, immersive worldbuilding that makes the city feel alive and keeps you coming back for more. What sets it apart, though, is the emotional connection you form with the characters - every decision and conversation feels heavy, meaningful, and grounded. Throughout the entire gameplay loop, you never feel like you are completing filler content just for the sake of checking off a box; every mission carries real narrative weight.

Then comes Phantom Liberty—the ultimate cherry on top. Easily ranking among the best expansion packs ever created, it kicks off with a bang and maintains non-stop momentum straight through to the end.

Seeing where Cyberpunk 2077 started compared to where it sits today is nothing short of incredible. CDPR delivered a legendary gameplay experience, and getting to step into the shoes of V is an journey no RPG fan should miss

Most of the time the game just feels like GTA with the Cyberpunk name slapped on it. If you're hoping for something relatively faithful to the tabletop experience, you're probably going to be disappointed. If you're looking for a relatively generic open world shooter, you might be somewhat satisfied... provided you can look at the copious amounts of bugs and blatantly half baked mechanics. Despite the fanbase's claims that CDProjekt has totally fixed everything, I constantly ran into issues. It feels like every other time I'd try to call up my car it'd just spawn 30 feet in the air and land upside down. AI is still generally atrocious. Stealth and hacking are complete afterthoughts, and most of the time the gunplay is just awful.
